knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The procedure requires the customer's permission before the computer is switched off and unplugged.
Computer equipment is sensitive to dust, water and silicone-based polish, so these must be kept away from it. The other options are not in the procedure.
The solution is applied to the cloth, which is then used to wipe the keys. Spraying or pouring solution onto the equipment is not allowed.

practicalCriteria: Learner checks the scope of a supplied job card, and records whether the computer equipment is in scope before touching it.
Learner asks permission, switches off a supplied mock computer at the mains and unplugs it, with no water near the equipment.
Learner cleans a supplied keyboard with a mini vacuum or soft brush, applies solution to the cloth only, and cleans between the keys with a damp cotton bud.
Learner returns every item moved during the job to its place and plugs the mock computer back in, observed by the assessor.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Scope confirmation recorded on the job card
Assessor observation of the mock keyboard and screen clean
Record of items moved and returned
stopWorkCriteria: Computer equipment is not in scope and the learner starts cleaning it anyway
Liquid has entered the equipment or a power point has been wetted
Customer has not given permission to switch off and unplug
Equipment is damaged, or a fault is found
